subject: Chemistry
description: pH, neutralisation, indicators, buffers, everyday chemistry

questions.stem: The pH of a NEUTRAL solution at 25 °C is:
questions.explanation: At 25 °C, pure water auto-ionises such that [H⁺] = [OH⁻] = 10⁻⁷ M → pH = −log10⁻⁷ = 7. pH < 7 is acidic, pH > 7 is basic. (At higher temperatures neutral pH drops slightly below 7 because Kw increases.)
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: Which of the following is a STRONG acid?
questions.explanation: HCl fully ionises in water (Ka → very large). Acetic, carbonic and citric acids are weak (partial ionisation). Other strong acids: H₂SO₄, HNO₃, HBr, HI, HClO₄.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: Blue litmus paper turns RED when dipped in a solution of:
questions.explanation: Acids turn blue litmus red. Lemon juice (citric acid) is acidic. NaOH, baking soda (NaHCO₃) and soap are alkaline — they turn red litmus blue.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: Match the COMMON NAME with its chemical formula. A. Baking soda  B. Washing soda  C. Caustic soda  D. Bleaching powder. List-II: 1. NaOH  2. NaHCO₃  3. Ca(OCl)Cl / CaOCl₂  4. Na₂CO₃·10H₂O.
questions.explanation: Baking soda = sodium hydrogen-carbonate NaHCO₃. Washing soda = sodium carbonate deca-hydrate Na₂CO₃·10H₂O. Caustic soda = sodium hydroxide NaOH. Bleaching powder = calcium hypochlorite chloride CaOCl₂ (Ca(OCl)Cl).

questions.stem: Consider the following about ACID RAIN. 1. It is caused mainly by sulphur dioxide (SO₂) and oxides of nitrogen (NOₓ) emitted from fossil-fuel burning. 2. The typical pH range of acid rain is 4.2–5.0. 3. It damages marble monuments like the Taj Mahal because calcium carbonate reacts with acids. 4. Liming of lakes is one mitigation measure. Which are correct?
questions.explanation: All four correct. SO₂ + H₂O → H₂SO₃, further oxidised to H₂SO₄; NOₓ → HNO₃. Natural rain is pH ~5.6; acid rain drops below ~5. Marble (CaCO₃) + H₂SO₄ → CaSO₄ + H₂O + CO₂ — 'marble cancer'. Liming (adding Ca(OH)₂ / CaCO₃) neutralises acidified lakes.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: When an acid reacts with a metal carbonate, the products are:
questions.explanation: Acid + carbonate → salt + CO₂↑ + H₂O. Example: 2HCl + Na₂CO₃ → 2NaCl + CO₂ + H₂O. Effervescence of CO₂ turns lime-water milky — the classic school test.
